add.title: Resolução CNJ n. 348 de 13/10/2020 (alterada pela Resolução n. 366/2021) — diretrizes para o tratamento da população LGBTI custodiada ou privada de liberdade (Conselho Nacional de Justiça)
add.summary: Brazil's National Council of Justice (CNJ) Resolution 348 of 13 Oct 2020, as amended by Resolution 366 of 20 Jan 2021, is the national framework for where LGBTI people who are arrested or imprisoned are housed: a person is recognised as LGBTI for these purposes by self-declaration before a judge, including at a custody hearing (Art. 4º); on arrest, the place of deprivation of liberty is fixed by a judge in a reasoned decision after the person is consulted about their preference (Art. 7º), and the judge must inform them of the available male, female and LGBTI-specific units and ask trans, travesti and intersex people whether they prefer custody in a female, male or specific unit, and within it general population or specific wings/cells (Art. 8º); the declared preference is recorded and a later change of placement is possible, with transfers prioritised in cases of violence or serious threat (Art. 9º). LGBTI-specific living spaces may not be used as disciplinary isolation, and compulsory transfer as punishment is prohibited (Art. 11, VI–VII). The resolution entered into force after publication (120 days, extended to 180 days by Res. 366/2021).

add.title: Elas também não são mulheres?: Travestis e mulheres transexuais em situação de prisão no Rio de Janeiro (Dilemas — Revista de Estudos de Conflito e Controle Social 17(2), 2024, e60615)
add.summary: Peer-reviewed census study (Alves-da-Silva & Bonan, Dilemas 17(2), 2024; lead author also of the LGBTI health division of the Rio de Janeiro state penitentiary administration, SEAP-RJ) of travestis and transgender women in prison in Rio de Janeiro state: 138 self-declared travesti/trans-woman inmates were interviewed inside eleven units deemed 'masculine' in the metropolitan region (April–June 2021, via the SEAP's SIPEN database). It documents that in the Rio state system travestis and trans women are housed in units treated as masculine, with some held in so-called 'neutral' or 'security' units, and frames male-unit placement as a double punishment combined with recurring basic-rights violations; it also cites the 2015 Rio de Janeiro state law granting them parity of treatment with cisgender women in women's units (hair length, feminine clothing, accessories and cosmetics) and national norms (2014; 2020) that let them be housed where they choose, including in units denominated masculine.
